# `Q-9-2` — Unexpected End of XML Input

> The XML document ended before the parser had finished what it
> was reading.

## What this means

The parser hit end-of-input mid-construct: an open element with
no closing tag, an attribute value missing its closing quote, a
comment with no `-->`, an entity reference with no `;`. The
message names what the parser was expecting when the input ran
out.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A truncated download** — the file was not fully written.
- **A missing closing tag** at the end of the document.
- **An unterminated comment, CDATA section, or processing
  instruction**: the parser is still inside one of those when
  the input ends.

## How to fix

Add the missing closing construct (`</tag>`, `-->`, `]]>`, or
the closing quote) at the appropriate place. If you suspect a
truncation, compare the file size with the source and re-fetch
if needed.

## Related

- `Q-9-1` — general XML syntax error: covers the same family of
  malformed input.
- `Q-9-3` — mismatched end tag, a related but distinct case
  where a closing tag *was* found but did not match the open
  one.
